probe.name: valgrind (installed for the run; Debian's 3.19.0 matches the fixture version)
probe.cmd: apt-get -qq update >/dev/null && apt-get -qq install -y valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; valgrind --version

build.name: compile five fixtures with pthreads, unmodified
build.cmd: for t in tc01_simple_race tc05_simple_race tc09_bad_unlock tc13_laog1 tc19_shadowmem; do gcc -O0 -g -pthread -w -o $BODY/build/$t $t.c || echo FAIL $t; done; ls $BODY/build | tr '\n' ' '

runs.name: RACE: tc01_simple_race natively (completes, error invisible) then under helgrind (Possible data race reported at the planted line)
runs.cmd: apt-get -qq update >/dev/null && apt-get -qq install -y valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; $BODY/build/tc01_simple_race; echo native_exit=$?; valgrind --tool=helgrind -q $BODY/build/tc01_simple_race 2>&1 | grep -E 'Possible data race|tc01_simple_race.c:|by thread|ERROR SUMMARY' | head -8; grep -c 'Possible data race' tc01_simple_race.stderr.exp

runs.name: LOCK ORDER (deadlock precursor): tc13_laog1 -- two threads take two locks in opposite orders; helgrind's lock-order graph reports the inversion
runs.cmd: apt-get -qq update >/dev/null && apt-get -qq install -y valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; valgrind --tool=helgrind -q $BODY/build/tc13_laog1 2>&1 | grep -E 'lock order|violated|acquired|ERROR SUMMARY' | head -8; grep -c 'lock order' tc13_laog1.stderr.exp

runs.name: BAD UNLOCK: tc09_bad_unlock -- unlocking a mutex the thread does not hold / an unlocked mutex
runs.cmd: apt-get -qq update >/dev/null && apt-get -qq install -y valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1; valgrind --tool=helgrind -q $BODY/build/tc09_bad_unlock 2>&1 | grep -E 'unlock|not locked|ERROR SUMMARY' | head -6
